record.original_question: Can the smoothness restrictions in KAM-based non-transitivity and non-mixing results for the three-dimensional Euler equation be relaxed, proving those dynamical properties in full generality?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Euler equations for an ideal incompressible fluid on a closed Riemannian 3-manifold $M$,
$$\partial_t u + \nabla_u u = -\nabla p, \qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
viewed as a dynamical system on the space $\mathcal{X}^k(M)$ of $C^k$ (or $C^{k,\alpha}$) divergence-free vector fields on $M$, preserving the energy $E(u) = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_M |u|^2\,d\mu$ and the helicity $\mathcal{H}(u) = \int_M u \wedge du$.

The flow $\Phi_t$ defined by this PDE is said to be:
- transitive on $\mathcal{X}^k(M)$ if there exists an initial datum whose orbit is dense;
- mixing on $\mathcal{X}^k(M)$ if for every pair of nonempty open sets $U,V \subset \mathcal{X}^k(M)$ there exists $T$ such that $\Phi_t(U) \cap V \neq \emptyset$ for all $t \geq T$.

It is known, via KAM-type arguments applied to the vorticity, that the Euler flow fails to be transitive and fails to be mixing on $\mathcal{X}^k(M)$ provided $k$ is sufficiently large and non-integer (typically $k > 4$, $k \notin \mathbb{Z}$), at any prescribed helicity value and sufficiently large energy.

Problem. Determine whether these non-transitivity and non-mixing properties of the 3D Euler dynamics persist for low-regularity spaces of vector fields (in particular, in the $C^1$ topology or with the weakest possible smoothness assumptions), thereby establishing the dynamical properties in full generality without the high-regularity restrictions inherent in the KAM approach.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has reduced the regularity requirements substantially. Cardona, Miranda, Peralta-Salas and others (e.g., "Global, Local and Dense Non-mixing of the 3D Euler Equation", Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 2020, and "The Euler non-mixing made easy", arXiv:2402.08836, 2024) prove non-mixing of the 3D Euler flow in the $C^1$ topology on smooth divergence-free vector fields, using contact/symplectic geometry rather than KAM. This relaxes the $C^k$, $k>4$ non-integer, restriction of the original KAM-based theorems. The full generality (e.g., in even lower regularity such as $L^p$ or Hölder $C^{0,\alpha}$ classes relevant to weak solutions) remains not fully settled, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The Euler non-mixing made easy
status_evidence.snippet: The time-dependent Euler equations are non-mixing on the space of smooth volume-preserving vector fields endowed with the C^1-topology, for any fixed helicity and large enough energy, solving a problem posed by Khesin, Misiolek, and Shnirelman.
status_evidence.claim: Non-mixing in C^1 topology is now established, lowering the smoothness requirement from the KAM-based result.

status_evidence.title: Contact type solutions and non-mixing of the 3D Euler equations
status_evidence.snippet: Using contact-type vorticity invariants allows non-mixing results with k ≥ 1, in contrast to the KAM approach requiring k > 4.
status_evidence.claim: Lower-regularity non-mixing results have been obtained via contact geometry, partially resolving the relaxation problem.

status_evidence.title: Global, Local and Dense Non-mixing of the 3D Euler Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Non-mixing of the 3D Euler equation in C^k topology for k>4 non-integer.
status_evidence.claim: The original KAM-based non-mixing theorem requires high regularity (k>4 non-integer).
